Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the paper visibly inside the cup, with evidence it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on the rim?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the paper placed inside the cup and visibly stuffed into it. Fail if the paper is only nearby or on the rim, or the image shows no progress toward placing it inside. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is inside and stuffed.
node.binding: Assess only the requested paper-in-cup edit, using the image evidence; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding the paper near the cup, but the paper is not visibly inside or stuffed into it.

fulfillment: The current binding is truncated/ambiguous and omits the source-to-edit comparison, while the node’s fuller criteria correctly distinguish absent from partial progress. Preserve that distinction: assess whether the requested paper-to-cup placement changed relative to the source, and count only observable progress toward putting the paper into the cup—not unrelated edits or mere proximity. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue card-like object, with no visible cup; the source shows a white paper and blue cup. This supports no evidenced progress, but the missing/changed objects make the target comparison less secure than the traces’ high confidence suggests. Ensure the node can return unknown when the target objects or their relation cannot be reliably identified, rather than treating an unobservable target as confidently absent. The checks executed successfully, so this is a visual-evidence/binding issue, not a transport or dependency failure.

Preserve the existing pass/fail/unknown distinction: return unknown when the paper or cup cannot be reliably identified or their relation cannot be judged; do not treat missing or changed-looking objects as confident evidence that no progress occurred. In this pair, the source shows a white paper and blue cup, while the edit shows a hand holding a blue card-like object and no clearly identifiable cup. That supports no *visible* progress, but makes the comparison uncertain, so the trace’s high confidence is not warranted. The checks ran successfully; this is a binding/evidence and confidence-calibration issue, not a transport or dependency failure.
